judgements.referenceQuote: President and CEO, Walmart, Inc.In officeFebruary 2014 – January 2026Preceded byMike DukeSucceeded byJohn Furner
judgements.evidenceQuote: In November 2025, Walmart announced McMillon would retire as CEO in January 2026 after almost 12 years as CEO and over 40 years with the company. He retired in January 2026.
judgements.rationale: Dossier states he became CEO effective February 1, 2014 (claims 59b6595c, 2b70cfc0), retired as CEO in January 2026 (this claim), and that he 'will be succeeded by John Furner on February 1, 2026' (c8965e87), together matching the full reference fact.

judgements.referenceQuote: led the company's Sam's Club division, from 2005 to 2009, and Walmart International, from 2009 to 2013
judgements.evidenceQuote: from 2005 to 2009 he served as president and CEO of Sam’s Club
judgements.rationale: Sam's Club 2005–2009 is stated exactly, and Walmart International leadership is stated (22430e05: 'From February of 2009 to 2014, Doug served as president and CEO of Walmart International'), but the International end date is given as 2014 rather than 2013, so the full fact is only partially recovered.

judgements.referenceQuote: He began his Walmart career in 1984 as an hourly associate
judgements.evidenceQuote: He started out in 1984 as a summer associate in the Walmart distribution center
judgements.rationale: Same fact: 1984 start as a summer associate in a Walmart distribution centre; the 'unloading trucks' detail is elaboration, not a change of subject, scope or dates.

judgements.referenceQuote: It invested heavily in people by increasing wages, expanding parental leave and funding education opportunities. Walmart also lowered its prices, built a large eCommerce business and embraced technology to improve customer and associate experiences
judgements.evidenceQuote: In February 2015, he announced raising associate minimum wage to $9/hour this year and $10 next year
judgements.rationale: The dossier covers increased wages (this claim and 39fcee91, 572d6c5d) and omnichannel strategy (dc5ab5be), but does not state expanded parental leave, funded education opportunities, lowered prices, or a large eCommerce business as part of Walmart's account of his tenure.

judgements.referenceQuote: Doug also served on the boards of Business Roundtable and the Consumer Goods Forum
judgements.evidenceQuote: he serves on the board of directors of the Consumer Goods Forum, the US-China Business Council and Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art
judgements.rationale: Consumer Goods Forum board membership is stated, and Walmart board service is stated (7bfae9e8: 'He has served on the board of directors for Walmart since 2013'), but Business Roundtable is not mentioned anywhere in the dossier.

judgements.referenceQuote: McMillon attended University of Arkansas, where he graduated with a  Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in accounting in 1989
judgements.evidenceQuote: McMillon obtained their Bachelor of Science in Business Administration from the University of Arkansas in 1989
judgements.rationale: The BSBA from the University of Arkansas in 1989 is stated, and the MBA from the University of Tulsa is stated (a417ddd21), but the accounting major is not mentioned, so the degree fact is only partially recovered.

judgements.referenceQuote: Doug McMillon is a lifelong merchant
judgements.rationale: No dossier statement describes him as 'a lifelong merchant' or any similar self-reported characterisation.

judgements.referenceQuote: McMillon was born in Memphis, Tennessee,[5] and grew up in Jonesboro, Arkansas,[6] the eldest of three children born to Laura and Morris McMillon, a dentist who served in Vietnam
judgements.rationale: The dossier contains only 'Bentonville, United States' (ba1830bb), which does not state that he was born in Memphis, grew up in Jonesboro, was the eldest of three children, or moved to Bentonville at 16.

overclaims.statement: Doug McMillon serves as President & CEO of Walmart since February 2009
overclaims.citedQuote: Doug McMillon serves as President & CEO of Walmart since February 2009
overclaims.rationale: Asserts McMillon 'serves as' President & CEO of Walmart since February 2009. Both the start date (he became CEO Feb 1, 2014) and the present tense are wrong; he retired January 2026 and John Furner succeeded him.

overclaims.statement: Doug McMillon is the CEO of Walmart.
overclaims.rationale: States in present tense that McMillon is the CEO of Walmart, but he retired on 31 January 2026 and was succeeded by John Furner on February 1, 2026.

overclaims.statement: Doug McMillon is president and chief executive officer of Walmart
overclaims.citedQuote: Doug McMillon (IG: @dougmcmillon) is president and chief executive officer of Walmart
overclaims.rationale: Present-tense claim that McMillon is president and CEO of Walmart; the dossier's own retained sources give his January 2026 retirement and Furner's succession.

overclaims.statement: Doug McMillon, who has been with the retailer for 15 years, will retire and will be replaced by John Furner.
overclaims.rationale: Says McMillon 'has been with the retailer for 15 years,' contradicting the well-supported record that he joined in 1984 and spent over 40 years with the company.

overclaims.statement: Doug McMillon pulled the plug on AR-15s and other scary looking rifles for Walmart.
overclaims.citedQuote: Doug was the guy who pulled the plug on AR-15s and other scary looking rifles, deciding that Walmart wouldn't sell those types of rifles any longer.
overclaims.rationale: Attributes Walmart's rifle-sales decision solely to McMillon personally ('Doug was the guy who pulled the plug'), based on a partisan podcast; the company decision is framed as his unilateral personal act, echoing the flagged wage-credit pattern of company action recast as personal execution.

overclaims.statement: Walmart CEO Doug McMillon keeps fending off Amazon for the top spot on the Fortune 500.
overclaims.citedQuote: Walmart CEO Doug McMillon keeps fending off Amazon for the top spot on the Fortune 500.
overclaims.rationale: Present-tense framing of McMillon as sitting Walmart CEO fending off Amazon comes from a June 2024 article; he has since retired, so presenting it as current is stale.

overclaims.statement: He has served on the board of directors for Walmart since 2013 and is currently the chair of the executive and global compensation committees
overclaims.citedQuote: He has served on the board of directors for Walmart since 2013 and is currently the chair of the executive and global compensation committees
overclaims.rationale: Claims he 'is currently the chair of the executive and global compensation committees' of Walmart's board, sourced from a 2018 podcast bio; after his January 2026 retirement this 'currently' is at best stale and unverified.

usefulness.rationale: The dossier gives a clear picture of who Doug McMillon is: Walmart hourly associate from 1984, CEO February 2014 to January 2026, succeeded by John Furner, with wage investments, e-commerce buildout, and gun-policy decisions during his tenure. However, it is cluttered with contradictory and stale claims (CEO 'since 2009', 'is the CEO' present tense, '15 years with the retailer') that a reader must reconcile, and it does not explicitly flag what it does not know (e.g., his post-CEO Fed task force role appears only in thin citations). Good enough to prepare for a meeting if the reader heeds the contested/stale flags, but not self-evidently complete.
